summary: DELTA CLAIM VERIFIED, NOT TAKEN ON TRUST. `git diff f24e3ac6f64ff93af91921729a70a71f6d38351e --cached` (the tree my round-3 verdict is bound to) is one file, one insertion: baselines/review.txt +1. No test file, no source file, no golden changed. The 14-test mutation matrix from round 3 therefore carries over unaltered and was NOT re-run: while->if dies only in legalPipeliningAtDepthTHREEIsPERMITTED; watermark keyed on 0L dies in aSUCCESSORChainAckingOutOfOrderIsCaught and TWOChainsAtDIFFERENTFloorsAreJudgedSeparately; base flattened to a global min dies in TWOChainsAtDIFFERENTFloorsAreJudgedSeparately; `+ w` -> the chain floor dies in theMessageNamesTheLOWESTUnconfirmedWriteNotTheFloor; the six round-1/round-2 watermark mutations all die. THE ARGUMENT IS SOUND AND ITS FACTS CHECK OUT. Its 'no seam' claim is not the overstatement M0.79's entry had to correct: the only mechanical seam is tests-only -- the four tests round 3 added against unchanged production -- and that IS the split the entry names ('the predicate' and 'the cases that pin it'). Landing on it would put the checker in the tree with the ten tests review MEASURED leaving three mutations alive, which is this row's own stated trap. FOUR FACTUAL CLAIMS CHECKED AGAINST THE RECORDED VERDICTS, all accurate: round 1's literal-0 base silent across a failover (reviewer d355d7f8, 'checkAckOrder drops the chain I5 is scoped to') and false-positive off base 0 (test-reviewer d355d7f8, MEASURED two violations on a 2-ack trace based at 1); 'a serial writer based at 1000 reported four' is a DIFFERENT fixture from the notes' 'reported two' and I verified it against the round-1 source at tree 778ca6e102e3 -- that loop scans `for (long lower = 0; lower < e.sequence(); lower++)` and breaks on the first miss, so a 4-ack serial trace based at 1000 yields exactly 4, one per ack; round 2's per-epoch watermark unconstrained (3e8198a5 major) and depth 3 only on the violation side (3e8198a5 major); round 3 nothing new in the delta and the production half verified by git diff that no logic moved (reviewer 55efbfba: one hunk in Invariants.java, 14 javadoc lines, no deletions). ONE MINOR CARRIES FORWARD, unchanged and still non-blocking, with a note on where it is recorded.

findings.title: The own-write arm's message is still unpinned, and the tree carries no pointer to that fact where M4.13 will read
findings.failure_scenario: Two legs. (1) The original harm, unchanged from round 3: M4.13 feeds a failing seed's trace in and the sweep reports 'epoch 2 acked sequence 2 while its own write was unconfirmed' when the ack was of sequence 7. The violation is still counted so the seed still fails, but the engineer pinning it as a named regression test is sent to the wrong slot. This is exactly the harm theMessageNamesTheLOWESTUnconfirmedWriteNotTheFloor was added to prevent on the sibling arm; the symmetric arm has no such test. (2) Discoverability: M4.11's two OTHER deferrals to M4.13 -- emit a confirmed event for the slot-0 CONTINUE, and run both checkers -- are staged under `### M4.13` in backlog-notes.md, which is where the M4.13 row's own link sends its reader. This one is not there. The commit body is not in the staged bytes (.git/COMMIT_EDITMSG still holds M0.86), so I cannot verify its content; what I can verify is that the path an M4.13 engineer actually walks -- backlog.md row -> backlog-notes.md#m413 -- does not carry it, and nobody picking up M4.13 runs `git log` for M4.11. The assertion then never gets added and the mutation below survives indefinitely.
findings.surviving_mutation: In the first arm of checkAckOrder, replace `+ e.sequence() +` with `+ e.epoch() +` in the message: `new Violation("I5", "epoch " + e.epoch() + " acked sequence " + e.epoch() + " while its own write was unconfirmed")`. MEASURED in the reviewer tree at round 3, and the arm is byte-identical at this hash: all 14 AckOrderTest tests pass. ackingAWriteThatWasNEVERConfirmedIsAVIOLATION asserts only invariant()=="I5"; ONECHAINSConfirmationsDoNotSatisfyANOTHERS asserts only that detail contains "epoch 2", which the mutant still produces; anAckThatIsBothUnconfirmedAndOutOfOrderCountsONCE asserts only hasSize(1). No test in the file asserts 'acked sequence <n>' on this arm.
findings.note: Non-blocking and it should NOT be fixed in a fifth round -- the arm is round-1 code that already carries a verdict, and a fix here creates a fresh surface. The cheapest close is one line under `### M4.13` in backlog-notes.md alongside its two siblings, and if the commit body is the only home the author wants, that is acceptable but weaker than where the sibling deferrals went.
